title: An Integrated Analysis of Manganese Metabolism-Related Genes and Their Association With Biomarkers, Immune Infiltration, and Clinical Subtypes in Alzheimer's Disease.
authors: Shu, Shengnan; Hu, Jiahao; Hu, Shanshan; Yao, Yefeng
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过机器学习分析阿尔茨海默病中锰代谢相关基因与免疫浸润及临床亚型，虽涉及转录因子调控网络构建，但核心非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，且无AI/物理模拟方法用于结合机制研究，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), a neurodegenerative condition marked by amyloid-beta plaques and tau protein neurofibrillary tangles, progresses against a backdrop of essential biological processes. Manganese, an indispensable trace element for vital functions including energy metabolism and antioxidant defense, is integral to neurological health. Its precise metabolic role throughout the course of AD pathogenesis is not fully elucidated. Four essential manganese metabolism-related genes were identified as diagnostic markers through a multi-omic framework. This approach integrated Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis with machine learning ensembles (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator/Random Forest/Extreme Gradient Boosting), followed by rigorous testing in an independent dataset. Beyond identification, we utilized CIBERSORT and ssGSEA to characterize immune infiltration and leveraged GSEA/GO/KEGG for pathway elucidation. Finally, AD patients were stratified into molecular subgroups based on these hub genes, and their underlying regulatory networks involving miRNAs and transcription factors were reconstructed. An integrated bioinformatics framework identified 12 differentially expressed genes related to manganese metabolism in AD. Machine-learning-based feature selection further pinpointed four key diagnostic biomarkers (TSPO, PTBP1, GLO1, and ACACB) with high discriminative power (AUC: 0.831-0.905). Immune infiltration analysis revealed substantial immune remodeling in AD, including an elevation of naive B cells. Moreover, AD samples were classified into two molecular subtypes displaying distinct immune and metabolic characteristics, and regulatory miRNA/TF interaction networks were constructed for the core genes. Our results shed new light on the molecular mechanisms underlying AD and support future efforts toward early diagnosis and personalized therapeutic interventions based on molecular subtypes.
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是一种以淀粉样蛋白-β斑块和tau蛋白神经原纤维缠结为特征的神经退行性疾病，其进展伴随着一系列关键生物过程。锰是能量代谢和抗氧化防御等重要功能所必需的微量元素，对神经健康至关重要。其在AD发病全过程中的精确代谢作用尚未完全阐明。通过多组学框架，我们确定了四个与锰代谢相关的关键基因作为诊断标志物。该方法整合了加权基因共表达网络分析（Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis）与机器学习集成（最小绝对收缩和选择算子/随机森林/极端梯度提升），并在独立数据集中进行了严格测试。除识别外，我们利用CIBERSORT和ssGSEA表征免疫浸润，并借助GSEA/GO/KEGG进行通路解析。最后，基于这些核心基因将AD患者分层为分子亚型，并重建了涉及miRNA和转录因子的潜在调控网络。一个整合的生物信息学框架在AD中识别出12个与锰代谢相关的差异表达基因。基于机器学习的特征选择进一步确定了四个关键诊断生物标志物（TSPO、PTBP1、GLO1和ACACB），具有高区分能力（AUC：0.831-0.905）。免疫浸润分析揭示了AD中显著的免疫重塑，包括初始B细胞的升高。此外，AD样本被分为两个显示不同免疫和代谢特征的分子亚型，并为核心基因构建了调控性miRNA/TF相互作用网络。我们的结果为AD的分子机制提供了新见解，并支持未来基于分子亚型的早期诊断和个性化治疗干预努力。
